From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ian Fletcher <ian.fletcher@tidewater.ai>, procurement@tidewater.ai
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer proposal: Tidewater pilot + staged expansion

Ian / Tidewater procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a draft AWS Marketplace private offer that structures a 3-month pilot (reduced unit price + activation credits) with an optional auto-conversion into a 12-month committed contract if Tidewater hits the agreed usage thresholds.

Key asks for your side:
- Confirm pilot scope (three business units identified in the SOW)
- Procurement approval window (we propose a 10 business-day review for the pilot PO)
- CFO primary signer and expected procurement checklist items (SOC2 report, data retention clause)

What we (Redwood) are proposing in the private offer:
- Pilot term: 3 months, 60% list price for tokens used up to agreed cap
- Activation credits: $25k applied at activation to cover onboarding/initial traffic
- Auto-convert option: upon passing usage gates, converts to 12-month commitment with a 15% incremental discount and co-sell credits for joint GTM activities

Attached: Tidewater-MAP-PO-Draft.pdf and a short pilot-performance-metrics.xlsx that outlines the thresholds. Vanessa and Vivek are looped in for legal/finance clearance.

Next step: If procurement confirms the 10-business-day review window, I’ll submit the private offer via AWS Marketplace and share the DocuSign link for the pilot PO.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Neha —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear structure. A few immediate procurement items before we can route to CFO: 
- Please confirm SOC 2 type II report and the date of last audit (we need within 12 months).
- Data retention and deletion clause: Tidewater requires a max 90-day ephemeral retention for derivatives used in production. Is that compatible?
- Can activation credits be split across two cost centers? We have separate BU finance owners.

Also, our procurement team needs the pilot PO to explicitly note the approval window; 10 business days is OK but we may push for 15 depending on our internal calendar. I’ll check with our legal and come back with any redlines.

Ian Fletcher
Head of Data Platforms
Tidewater Analytics
ian.fletcher@tidewater.ai

Ian / team —

Quick clarifications from legal/ops side: 
1) SOC2: Redwood’s latest SOC2 Type II report completed 2027-04-10. I’ll attach the evidence pack to the DocuSign envelope if Tidewater confirms moving forward.
2) Data retention: 90-day ephemeral retention for production derivatives is acceptable; we will add explicit language to the SOW and the private offer terms.
3) Activation credits split: we can structure the credits to be allocated across two BU cost centers. Note that AWS Marketplace activation accounting will require a single billing owner for invoicing; we’ll provide a simple internal chargeback template to Tidewater finance.

On the approval window: 15 business days is reasonable if your legal needs it. However, to keep activation timelines tight we recommend a canary activation on a single BU within 10 bd while procurement/legal review proceeds for the broader pilot. That reduces time-to-value and keeps the private offer live in AWS.

Vivek, please confirm finance is OK with the split-credit approach and provide the standard chargeback template.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Marketplace & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Vanessa / Neha —

Thanks for the rapid clarifications. Procurement has two redline asks before we circulate to CFO for signature: 
1) Pilot term: change from 3 months to 9 months with a 30-day early-exit clause for poor performance. We want a slightly longer runway to evaluate downstream model drift with our traffic.
2) Auto-convert: rather than auto-convert, we’d prefer an opt-in conversion executed by Tidewater within 30 days of pilot completion, with a guaranteed conversion rate hold for 14 days to allow internal approvals.

If Redwood is open to those two changes we can get this to CFO and legal within 10 business days. SOC2 evidence referenced above looks fine to legal at first pass.

procurement@tidewater.ai
Tidewater Analytics Procurement

Procurement team —

Appreciate the concrete asks. Redwood can accept both changes with minor operational notes: 
- Pilot term: we’ll move to a 9-month pilot with a 30-day early-exit clause. Activation credits will be prorated across the first 90 days; remaining credits expire at the end of the pilot unless extended by mutual written consent.
- Auto-convert: we will change auto-convert to an opt-in conversion with a 14-day conversion-rate hold for procurement approvals. To preserve the co-sell incentives, we’ll hold the 15% expansion discount for 14 days post-pilot for your execution.

Next steps: I’ll update the PO and SOW to reflect those changes and submit a refreshed private offer to AWS Marketplace. Vanessa will include SOC2 artifacts in the DocuSign and Vivek will confirm the chargeback template. If all looks good, I’ll generate the DocuSign link and target AWS activation within 3 business days of signature.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Tidewater live.
